name: ROWLAND, the Hon. Michelle Anne

headline.note: Official sources establish supermarket, NRMA and Gilbert + Tobin employment, political staff work and several overlapping public or nonprofit governance appointments. They do not provide exact employment dates, substantive hours, leave or breaks. Study, political staff, governance appointments and elected office are excluded, and no private full-time years are inferred from year-only ranges or the senior-lawyer title. Follow-up adds exact Parklands retirement, Premier’s Council for Women and party-office records, and removes unsupported law-firm election-day cessation. Governance and party activity remain excluded from employment totals.

career_spells.evidence_note: Parliament records all three University of Sydney qualifications, and Rowland says she was studying law there in 1990. Degree commencement and completion dates, study loads and overlap with paid work remain unresolved. The2000–01 report records completed BA(Hons)/LLB and an LLM still in progress, so degrees must not be treated as concurrently completed in1990.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: The official occupation record gives 1987–1995. Rowland identifies a supermarket in Blacktown and says she worked as a checkout operator for eight years, including while studying. In a 2019 local interview she says the work was on nights and weekends while she put herself through high school and a university law degree. This supports a study-compatible work pattern but not weekly hours, substantive full-time status or continuous service. The supermarket, exact dates and leave remain unpublished.
career_spells.counting_note: The work is private-sector employment, but the unidentified employer, year-only dates and missing hours prevent a full-time duration calculation.

career_spells.employer: Office of Mark Latham MP (federal electorate office; payroll entity unresolved)
career_spells.evidence_note: Parliament records electorate-officer work from 1995 to 1999, and Rowland later described it as one of her first and most important roles. A contemporary Australian Financial Review author description identifies her as a member of Mark Latham's staff across the same 1995–1999 interval; combined with the official electorate-officer classification and federal-MP description, this resolves the officeholder and jurisdiction. Exact appointment dates, payroll entity/title, hours, leave and whether every part of the interval was based in the electorate office remain unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Political-staff employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: The official parliamentary and ministerial biographies identify NRMA Ltd and the 1999–2000 range. Exact dates, business unit, hours, leave and overlap with electorate-office work or legal admission are not published. The2000–01 report identifies the Corporate Affairs and Communications unit; exact hours and boundaries remain unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: The private employer is identified, but year-only dates and missing full-time evidence prevent an exact duration calculation.

career_spells.role: Senior lawyer specialising in competition and regulation in telecommunications, media and technology
career_spells.evidence_note: Official chronology supports 2000–2010. The FTO 2008–09 report contemporaneously identifies corporate regulatory and commercial communications practice at Gilbert + Tobin alongside governance appointments. Removed election day as unsupported employment cessation. Exact appointment, promotion and cessation dates, ordinary hours, leave and campaign overlap remain unresolved. A2September2003 Gilbert+Tobin fax in the ACCC public register identifies Rowland as the sender on an Optus regulatory matter, providing a contemporaneous observation of substantive client work. It does not establish a promotion date, weekly hours or a separate Optus employment contract.
career_spells.counting_note: Private employment is well supported, but a senior title and year-only range do not prove full-time status or an exact interval.

career_spells.evidence_note: Annual report dates appointment to 1 August 2000 and records attendance at all ten eligible meetings in 2000–01. Official biographies give end year2004. Remuneration, exact cessation and workload remain unknown; overlaps legal employment.
career_spells.counting_note: This governance appointment is visible but excluded from full-time employment totals; a director title does not establish substantive full-time work.

career_spells.evidence_note: Parliament and the Attorney-General's biography record councillor service from 2004 to 2008 and deputy-mayoral service from 2007 to 2008. Exact election and cessation days, allowances, workload and overlap with legal work are not established in the cited sources.
career_spells.counting_note: Local elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies give 2007 commencement year. The Trust’s 2009–10 financial statements identify retirement on 7 July 2010. FTO contemporaneous biography corroborates the overlapping non-executive appointment and legal practice. Remuneration bands are pooled across members and cannot establish her precise payment or workload; appointment day remains unresolved. The contemporaneous 2007–2008 financial statements explicitly list her appointment as 1 January 2008, the Trust activity commencement date. This differs from the retrospective official 2007 start year. Preserve that supported year pending clarification of appointment versus operational commencement or predecessor service; do not silently replace it or infer a reappointment. Day-level cessation remains7July2010. The new report pools remuneration and cannot establish her individual payment or hours.
career_spells.counting_note: The non-executive public governance role is excluded from full-time employment totals.

career_spells.employer: Our Lady of Mercy College Parramatta
career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies record the school directorship from 2008 to 2010. Exact appointment dates, legal entity, pay, workload and cessation are unresolved, and the role overlaps legal practice and other governance work. The contemporaneous FTO chair biography corroborates this school governance role during legal practice.
career_spells.counting_note: Nonprofit governance is excluded; the director title does not establish substantive paid full-time employment.

career_spells.employer: NSW Film and Television Office, trading as Screen NSW
career_spells.evidence_note: Official sources record the chair appointment from 2009 to 2010. Screen NSW identifies itself as the NSW Government screen agency. Exact appointment dates, remuneration, workload and cessation are unresolved. Agency annual reports corroborate her appointment following the previous chair’s December 2008 retirement and continuing chairmanship at 30 June 2010. Scheduled term expiry 31 December 2011 is not an actual cessation date; retain the official 2010 end year. Agency office opening hours are not her employment hours.
career_spells.counting_note: Public-sector governance is excluded from full-time employment totals absent evidence of a substantive employment appointment.

career_spells.role: Member of the House of Representatives for Greenway
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen roster and current official biographies establish continuous House service from the 21 August 2010 election.
career_spells.counting_note: Federal elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: FTO 2008–09 annual report identifies Rowland as a member of the Premier’s Council for Women. Precise appointment and cessation, remuneration, attendance and time commitment are not supplied; concurrent with legal practice and other governance roles.
career_spells.counting_note: Public advisory/governance appointment is not evidence of substantive full-time employment.

career_spells.role: Secretary; senior vice-president, Young Labor NSW
career_spells.evidence_note: Official parliamentary biography identifies these party offices without dates, remuneration or hours. They are separate from electorate-office employment; no paid organising appointment or full-time status inferred. NSW Young Labor’s own historical list identifies secretary service in 1996. This is a service-year observation, not an exact appointment or cessation date and not evidence for the separately recorded senior vice-presidency dates, remuneration or full-time status.
career_spells.counting_note: Excluded category; not added to public/private employment headlines.

career_spells.role: Secretary, ALP Lalor Park and Districts Branch
career_spells.evidence_note: Official parliamentary biography identifies these party offices without dates, remuneration or hours. They are separate from electorate-office employment; no paid organising appointment or full-time status inferred.
career_spells.counting_note: Excluded category; not added to public/private employment headlines.

career_spells.role: ALP national women’s network executive; NSW administrative committee and women’s forum; conference and electorate-council delegate
career_spells.evidence_note: Official parliamentary biography identifies these party offices without dates, remuneration or hours. They are separate from electorate-office employment; no paid organising appointment or full-time status inferred.
career_spells.counting_note: Excluded category; not added to public/private employment headlines.

career_spells.evidence_note: Public professional profile gives month boundaries. Remuneration and hours not stated; concurrent with parliamentary office.
career_spells.counting_note: Excluded category; not added to public/private employment headlines.

research_notes: Identify the Blacktown supermarket and obtain exact appointment/cessation dates, hours and leave; resolve how checkout work overlapped University of Sydney study.
Identify the employing parliamentarian and jurisdiction for the 1995–1999 electorate-officer role and obtain appointment dates, payroll title, hours and leave.

Obtain NRMA and Gilbert + Tobin employment records with exact dates, substantive hours, leave, promotions and 2010 campaign overlap; do not infer full-time status from the senior-lawyer title or ten-year narrative.

Obtain appointment instruments, remuneration and workloads for the Western Sydney Area Health Service, Western Sydney Parklands Trust, Our Lady of Mercy College and Screen NSW governance roles, plus exact Blacktown council dates. Missing evidence is not zero, and overlapping directorships must not be summed as full-time years.

2026-10-01 follow-up: Parklands Trust retirement resolved to 7 July 2010 from annual financial statements; newly documented Premier’s Council for Women and separate party offices; contemporaneous legal/governance overlap and historical Screen NSW entity clarified. Gilbert + Tobin end restored to supported 2010 year precision.

Searched employer/alumni references, supermarket names, electorate-officer identity, ordinary full-time hours, historical FTO/Screen NSW/Communities annual reports and public profiles. No reliable supermarket name, employing parliamentarian, NRMA business unit, private-employment hours or leave found. Namesake profiles and other workers’ hours excluded.

Next leads: NSW appointment gazettes and Premier’s Council membership reports, legal practice personnel records and contemporaneous electorate-office staff lists. Chair scheduled term through 2011 conflicts only if mistaken for actual tenure; do not extend service. Pooled director remuneration is not an individual salary.

Source access: NSW Parliament PDFs exposed indexed primary text but later page/screenshot retrieval returned HTTP500 redirect errors; government-data mirror timed out. Communities NSW financial statements remained readable and retirement entry was recovered. No term start back-calculated from nominal three-year appointment.

Second follow-up2October2026: health-service annual report materially narrows governance appointment and prior federal adviser/NRMA unit, plus LLM chronology; self-reported NSW Labor presidency added separately. Searches of supermarket identity,1996 university dates, electorate officeholder and NRMA full-time evidence did not resolve employer, hours or leave. Same-name medical alumni, beauty-business and US legal profiles excluded. Academic author-biography lead remains for qualification timing; party and board posts do not establish paid full-time service. Exact employment dates and overlaps remain priority gaps.

Third follow-up3October2026 resolves Mark Latham MP as the federal officeholder for the1995–1999 staff interval by combining the official electorate-officer chronology, the contemporaneous health-service reference to advising a federal MP and an AFR author description naming Latham. Exact appointment dates, payroll entity/title, hours, leave and whether the whole interval was electorate-office based remain unresolved. Searches did not identify the Blacktown supermarket or improve private-employment hours; no headline total changed.

Fourth follow-up4October2026 materially adds Rowland's first-person description of nights-and-weekends checkout work while funding high school and university law study. This supports a study-compatible work pattern and cautions against assuming full-time employment across1987–1995, but it does not provide weekly hours, exact dates, continuity, leave or the supermarket identity. Exact NRMA, Latham-office and board searches otherwise repeated official chronology; no headline total changed.

Follow-up2026-10-04: New primary party historical list resolves secretary service to an observation in1996 without manufacturing tenure boundaries or extending it to senior vice-presidency. Downloaded and text-searched the original NSW DPC2007–08 report: no Rowland match; generic women’s programmes do not establish her Premier’s Council appointment. Targeted admission/promotion and council searches returned existing biographies or namesakes, with no new legal employment hours or dates. Defer exhausted queries until a gazette, personnel record or council list is identified.

2026-10-05 follow-up found original2007–08 Parklands financial appointment table explicitly listing1January2008, conflicting with retrospective official2007 start. Added discrepancy and source without silently replacing supported chronology; precise cessation remains7July2010. Visually inspected original2September2003 ACCC-filed G+T fax identifying Rowland on Optus regulatory matter, corroborating substantive legal duties. No private employment hours or leave resolved. S1 date queries returned unrelated2007 pages; no appointment gazette found. NSW PDF screenshot returned500 redirected artifact inaccessible/non-retryable; readable original text retained, not treated as job-wide error.

Second targeted primary pass 2026-10-05: Tested Premier Council for Women appointment/gazette and Parklands commencement instrument queries, plus contemporary council-service sources. Both engines returned held FTO/Screen NSW biographies and the same original Parklands financial table, without a separate appointment instrument. Secondary encyclopaedia day-level council dates remain unsupported by an original instrument and were not adopted; community event report only corroborates already held service. Law-firm maternity/leave queries did not identify an attributable employment or leave record. Preserve the explicit 2007 versus 1 January 2008 Parklands discrepancy and unknown legal hours/leave; no new duration or fact. Useful next evidence is an actual appointment instrument, historical Council for Women roster or named employer personnel record, not another retrospective biography.

Third targeted pass2026-10-06: Tested Blacktown-supermarket identity, Premier’s Council for Women, NRMA and exact checkout-history routes. A first-person ministerial interview repeats eight years at an unnamed Blacktown supermarket, consistent with the official1987–1995 range and earlier nights/weekends account, but supplies no employer, weekly hours, precise dates or leave. Other results repeated official chronology and unrelated current supermarket/council events. No appointment instrument, private-work personnel record or new boundary emerged. Broad identity/date searches are exhausted pending a named employer record, gazette or personnel file; no fact or duration changed.
